prompt:
Rebase a stale branch onto current main and resolve the conflicts. This is re-integration work, not redesign.

BRANCH: fix/price-cache-reload-validation — 6 commits, ~952 insertions across 9 files, last touched 3 weeks ago. Coherent series: "harden cache reload and discovery", "track discovery flight success", "bound market discovery claims", "make discovery failure release atomic".

TASK: rebase it onto current main. `git merge-tree` reports 6 conflicts, all in the evaluator pricing path:
  crates/filler-evaluator/src/evaluator.rs
  crates/filler-evaluator/src/evaluator/impl_setup.rs
  crates/filler-evaluator/src/evaluator/token_pricing.rs
  crates/filler-evaluator/src/evaluator/token_pricing_helpers.rs
  crates/filler-evaluator/src/evaluator/token_pricing_tests.rs
  crates/filler-route-log/src/read.rs

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE: the branch rebased onto main, compiling, with the test suite green, and a short report saying for EACH conflict what the two sides wanted and which way you resolved it. If a conflict cannot be resolved without a judgement call about intended behaviour, STOP on that file and say so rather than guessing — a wrong resolution in the pricing path silently changes profit gating.

THINGS THAT WILL WASTE YOUR TIME IF YOU DO NOT KNOW THEM:
- A fresh git worktree has NO submodules. Run `git submodule update --init --recursive` first or cargo cannot even load the workspace manifest ("failed to load manifest for dependency fast-wallet").
- Every build must set RUSTC_WRAPPER="" (empty, not unset) or cargo dies with EPERM on dozens of crates. Use: RUSTC_WRAPPER="" CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 cargo test -p <crate> --lib
- Disk on this machine is tight. If a disk guard blocks a build, say so and stop; do not work around it.
- `cmd | tail; echo $?` reports tail exit code, not the build. Redirect to a log and check the real status.

RED LINES:
- Resolve conflicts only. Do NOT refactor, rename, reformat unrelated code, or "improve" either side.
- Do not drop either side of a conflict silently. If you take one side wholesale, say which and why.
- Run the tests. Paste real output. Never report a result you did not execute.
- No force-push, no git checkout of unrelated refs, no broadcasting anything.
- English only.
- Where this brief is silent, prefer the more conservative resolution and say what you chose.
After completing each major step, output on its own line: [MILESTONE] <brief description>
Do NOT add println!/console.log/print statements with [MILESTONE] to source code — milestones go in your conversation output only.
A milestone is progress, never a deliverable: never end your turn on a milestone line. Keep working until the requested final answer is written.
[Git Staging Rule — CHECK BEFORE EVERY COMMIT]
Before every `git commit`, run `git status --porcelain` and confirm zero `??` lines AND zero `M`/`MM` lines outside the staging area.
If any untracked files exist, stage them with `git add <file>` first.
If any tracked files are modified but unstaged, run `git add <file>` or `git add -u` first.
`git commit -a` and `git add -u` do NOT stage untracked files — always use `git add <newfile>` for new files.
A task that leaves untracked or unstaged files in the worktree will FAIL and the agent will be asked to re-commit. Repeat failure aborts the task with data-loss prevention.


--- Team Toolbox ---
The following tools are available via bash. Use `aid tool show <name>` for full usage.

  biome: Rust-powered linter+formatter for JS/TS/JSON. 25x faster than ESLint+Prettier. Usage: biome check <path>, biome format <path>, biome lint <path>
  deploy: Cross-compile smart-router for Linux, upload, restart service. Requires RUSTC_WRAPPER='' for zigbuild.
  just: Modern task runner (Make alternative). Usage: just [recipe] [args...], just --list, just --evaluate
